test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 01 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion(s) logically follow/s from the given statements.

Statements:

Some wigs are roses.

All roses are bugs.

Conclusions (I): Some wigs are bugs.

Conclusions (II): All bugs are roses.
solution:
Given Statements:

Some wigs are roses.

All roses are bugs.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4896873fdff05cc77ecfe4a8bee84dc341d2bf20f2730b9fc7d8bffbaa279c4c.png] 

Conclusions:

** (I) Some wigs are bugs:**

then those **same wigs (which are roses)** must also be **bugs**.
So, **Conclusion (I) follows**.

**(II) All bugs are roses:**

The statement says **all roses are bugs**, but it does **not** say that all bugs come from roses.
Thus, we **cannot** conclude that **all bugs are roses**.
So, **Conclusion (II) does NOT follow**.

So, **Only conclusion (I) follows.** 

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".
